evidence.claim: Cardholder C08106 disputes the $128.33 online charge 3583227 dated 2016-12-29 01:53:54.
Flagged charge is 3.63x the 180d mean of $35.31 (amount_z 3.36); a second out-of-pattern online charge of $92.86 (2.63x mean) occurred ~24h earlier, forming a 2-transaction burst within 48h.

Flagged transaction ran from 'unknown | unknown | firefox 47.0 | unknown', absent from the card's 180d device history, with identity device_new_flag = New and a hotmail.com email (prior-night txn used gmail.com).
Same card C08106-K1 has a prior confirmed card-not-present fraud (CC-3778, $58.42, 2016-09-20), showing the number was previously compromised.

Counter-evidence: the card shows 77 distinct devices across 209 online transactions in 180 days, so a previously unseen browser string is weak on its own; $128.33 is below the card's $138.89 historical max.
The firefox 47.0 profile appears on 6 cards all-time but only 1 card in this window, and links to high-fraud cards run through generic strings, so no shared-origin cluster is established.
Memory on this customer is mixed: CC-0696 on the same card was cleared after the cardholder confirmed travel, so a dispute is one signal, not proof.
Policy R2: a customer denial supports BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE; exposure of $221.19 is under $1,000 and no shared device cluster is shown, so no regulatory filing is required (§3a).
Assumed reply: customer also denies the $92.86 charge 3580804 and any new-device use that week.

case.summary: Cardholder C08106 disputes a $128.33 online charge (3583227) placed 2016-12-29 from a browser profile never seen on the card and flagged New by the identity record. The graph shows it is not isolated: a $92.86 online charge the previous night (3580804) is also well above the card's $35.31 average, giving a classic two-transaction CNP burst inside 48h. The same card already carries a confirmed CNP fraud from September (CC-3778). The card's habit of using many devices (77 in 180d) and the fact that $128.33 sits below its historical max keep this short of certainty on graph evidence alone, so the companion charge was put to the customer. With the customer denying both, the episode reads as card-not-present fraud from a new device: block the card, open a case, total exposure $221.19; no regulatory filing since exposure is under $1,000 and no rare shared-device or region cluster is established.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: Customer states they also do not recognise the $92.86 online charge from 2016-12-28 and did not use a Firefox browser or any new device that week.

initial.reason: §5/§6: p=0.70 is not decisive; verify before any block
§3a: a case is opened whenever evidence is requested
R1: keep the card active but raise monitoring while verification is pending

final.reason: R2: customer denies the transaction; exposure $221.19 <= $2,500 -> L1
R2/§3a: open the fraud case and write it to the graph

next_best_actions.what_changed: The customer's denial of the second $92.86 charge confirmed a two-transaction episode rather than one odd purchase, moving probability from 0.70 to 0.87 and settling the verdict as fraud.

sar.reason: Case only, no report: fraud with exposure $221.19 <= $1,000, no shared device/region link and a documented pattern, so no §3a condition holds.

stop_reason: Verdict is fraud at 0.87 with at least two independent pieces of evidence (customer denial of both charges, out-of-pattern 48h burst from a new device, prior confirmed fraud on the same card); further steps would not change the action.
